# Threads

## `Bead`

```python
Bead(document: Document, xref: int, generation: int = 0)
```

A handle on one bead dictionary of an article thread (ISO 32000-2 Table 163).

Properties read the current version of the document. `rect` converts
between `/R` in PDF user space and `page`'s display coordinates,
and assigning `page` or `rect` updates the bead (and pages'
`/B` arrays when moving across pages) in one transaction. A handle whose
bead or thread was removed raises `StaleObjectError`, and works
again if undo restores it.

### `Bead.document`

```python
Bead.document: Document
```

The document that holds this bead.

### `Bead.xref`

```python
Bead.xref: int
```

The bead's indirect object number.

### `Bead.obj`

```python
Bead.obj: Dictionary
```

The bead's dictionary in the low-level object model.

### `Bead.thread`

```python
Bead.thread: Thread
```

The `Thread` that owns this bead.

### `Bead.page`

```python
Bead.page: Page
```

The `Page` on which this bead appears (`/P`).

Settable.

### `Bead.rect`

```python
Bead.rect: Rect
```

The bead's rectangle in `page`'s display coordinates (`/R`).

Settable.

## `Beads`

```python
class Beads(Sequence[Bead])
Beads(thread: Thread)
```

The ordered sequence of `Bead` handles in a `Thread`, as `thread.beads` returns it.

Walks the circular `/F` -> `/N` bead ring iteratively up to 4,096 beads
with cycle detection. `add`, `move`, and `del thread.beads[i]`
each update the ring, `BeadFirst["T"]`, and pages' `/B` arrays in one
transaction. Deleting every bead of a thread raises `ValueError`;
remove the thread from `doc.threads` instead.

### `Beads.__getitem__`

```python
Beads.__getitem__(index: int | slice) -> Bead | list[Bead]
```

Return one bead, or a list of beads for a slice.

### `Beads.__len__`

```python
Beads.__len__() -> int
```

Return the number of beads in the thread.

### `Beads.__iter__`

```python
Beads.__iter__() -> Iterator[Bead]
```

Iterate over the thread's beads in reading order.

### `Beads.add`

```python
Beads.add(page: Page | int, rect: Sequence[float], *, index: int | None = None) -> Bead
```

Insert a new bead on `page` covering `rect` (in display coordinates) at `index`.

`index` is clamped like `list.insert`, appending when `None`.
Updates the circular `/N`/`/V` ring, `Thread["F"]` and
`BeadFirst["T"]` when inserted first, and `page["B"]` in one
transaction.

### `Beads.move`

```python
Beads.move(index: int, to: int)
```

Move bead `index` so that it ends at `to`, in one transaction.

### `Beads.__delitem__`

```python
Beads.__delitem__(index: int | slice)
```

Remove one bead or a slice of beads from the thread, in one transaction.

## `BeadSpecification`

```python
BeadSpecification(page: Page | int, rect: Rect | Sequence[float])
```

One bead to create inside an article thread: a page and a display-space rectangle.

`page` is a `Page` handle or a zero-based page index (negative
indexes count from the end when added to a document), and `rect` is a
non-empty `Rect` or 4-number sequence in that page's display
coordinates.

## `Thread`

```python
Thread(document: Document, xref: int, generation: int = 0)
```

A handle on an indirect article `Thread` dictionary in `Document.threads` (ISO 32000-2 Table 162).

`beads` exposes the circular bead ring, and `title`,
`author`, `subject`, `keywords`, `created`, and
`modified` read, set, and delete entries of the thread information
dictionary `/I` in one transaction each. A handle whose thread was
removed raises `StaleObjectError`, and works again if undo restores
it.

### `Thread.document`

```python
Thread.document: Document
```

The document that holds this thread.

### `Thread.xref`

```python
Thread.xref: int
```

The thread's indirect object number.

### `Thread.obj`

```python
Thread.obj: Dictionary
```

The thread's dictionary in the low-level object model.

### `Thread.beads`

```python
Thread.beads: Beads
```

The thread's ordered `Beads` sequence.

### `Thread.title`

```python
Thread.title: str | None
```

The thread's title (`/I /Title`), or `None`; `del` removes it.

Settable.

### `Thread.author`

```python
Thread.author: str | None
```

The thread's author (`/I /Author`), or `None`; `del` removes it.

Settable.

### `Thread.subject`

```python
Thread.subject: str | None
```

The thread's subject (`/I /Subject`), or `None`; `del` removes it.

Settable.

### `Thread.keywords`

```python
Thread.keywords: str | None
```

The thread's keywords (`/I /Keywords`), or `None`; `del` removes it.

Settable.

### `Thread.created`

```python
Thread.created: str | None
```

The thread's creation date (`/I /CreationDate`), or `None`; `del` removes it.

Settable.

### `Thread.modified`

```python
Thread.modified: str | None
```

The thread's modification date (`/I /ModDate`), or `None`; `del` removes it.

Settable.

## `ThreadAction`

```python
ThreadAction(thread: int | str, bead: int | None = None, *, file: str | None = None)
```

An action that begins reading an article thread (`/S /Thread`, ISO 32000-2 Table 209).

`thread` is a non-negative zero-based thread index or a non-empty thread
title (`/D`), `bead` is an optional non-negative zero-based bead index
within that thread (`/B`, defaulting to its first bead when `None`),
and `file` names an external PDF file when the thread lives in another
document (`/F`).

## `Threads`

```python
class Threads(Sequence[Thread])
Threads(document: Document)
```

The document's article threads in `Catalog["Threads"]` order, as `doc.threads` returns it.

Backed by an indirect `Catalog["Threads"]` array. `add`,
`move`, `del doc.threads[i]`, and `del doc.threads` each update
the catalog, bead rings, and pages' `/B` arrays in one transaction and
free unreferenced thread and bead objects.

### `Threads.__getitem__`

```python
Threads.__getitem__(index: int | slice) -> Thread | list[Thread]
```

Return one thread, or a list of threads for a slice.

### `Threads.__len__`

```python
Threads.__len__() -> int
```

Return the number of article threads in the document.

### `Threads.__iter__`

```python
Threads.__iter__() -> Iterator[Thread]
```

Iterate over the document's article threads.

### `Threads.add`

```python
Threads.add(
    beads: Iterable[BeadSpecification | tuple[Page | int, Sequence[float]]],
    *,
    index: int | None = None,
    title: str | None = None,
    author: str | None = None,
    subject: str | None = None,
    keywords: str | None = None,
    created: str | datetime | None = None,
    modified: str | datetime | None = None,
) -> Thread
```

Create an article thread from `beads` (at least one) and insert it at `index`.

Each item of `beads` is a `BeadSpecification` or a
`(page, rect)` pair in display coordinates. Optional metadata fields
populate the thread's `/I` dictionary; `created` and `modified`
accept either a PDF date string or a `datetime`.

### `Threads.move`

```python
Threads.move(index: int, to: int)
```

Move thread `index` so that it ends at `to`, in one transaction.

### `Threads.__delitem__`

```python
Threads.__delitem__(index: int | slice)
```

Remove one thread or a slice of threads, freeing unreferenced thread and bead objects.
